samuel2.19.p1.b1.text: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”

samuel2.19.p1.b2.text: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”

samuel2.19.p1.b3.text: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.

samuel2.19.p1.b4.text: “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”

samuel2.19.p2.b1.text: “Today you have disgraced all your servants …”

samuel2.19.p2.b2.text: “You love those who hate you and hate those who love you!”

samuel2.19.p2.b3.text: “Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, … if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight.”

samuel2.19.p2.b4.text: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king.

samuel2.19.p3.b1.text: “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.

samuel2.19.p3.b2.text: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle.

samuel2.19.p3.b3.text: So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”

samuel2.19.p4.b1.text: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king … You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood.’”

samuel2.19.p4.b2.text: “Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from this time you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!”

samuel2.19.p4.b3.text: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”

samuel2.19.p4.b4.text: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan.

samuel2.19.p5.b1.text: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David, along with a thousand men of Benjamin, …

samuel2.19.p5.b2.text: … as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan before the king

samuel2.19.p5.b3.text: “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing … here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”

samuel2.19.p6.b1.text: “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”

samuel2.19.p6.b2.text: “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, … Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”

samuel2.19.p7.b1.text: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king.

samuel2.19.p7.b2.text: He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.

samuel2.19.p7.b3.text: “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”

samuel2.19.p8.b1.text: “My lord the king, … because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me, and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king.”

samuel2.19.p8.b2.text: “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”

samuel2.19.p8.b3.text: “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!”

samuel2.19.p9.b1.text: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king … Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, … he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.

samuel2.19.p9.b2.text: “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”

samuel2.19.p9.b3.text: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

samuel2.19.p10.b1.text: “Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, …”

samuel2.19.p10.b2.text: “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”

samuel2.19.p10.b3.text: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.

samuel2.19.p10.b4.text: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.

samuel2.19.p11.b1.text: “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”

samuel2.19.p11.b2.text: “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”

samuel2.19.p11.b3.text: “We have ten shares in the king, … Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?”

samuel2.19.p11.b4.text: But the men of Judah pressed even harder than the men of Israel.
